title: The Impact of Façade Structure on the Natural Landscape: The Case of Contemporary Buildings in Poland at the Turn of the 21st Century
content: The article analyzes how the structure of the façade affects the integration of buildings with the natural landscape. The authors emphasize that contemporary architecture should harmoniously fit into the surroundings, not only in terms of technology and functionality, but also aesthetically and symbolically. The façade, as an "interface" between the building and the environment, is important in shaping the perception of the place, cultural identity and the relationship between users and the space. The article discusses four examples of modern single-family houses from different regions of Polish, which use local materials (brick, wood, stone) and simple, archetypal forms, creating a coherent relationship with the surrounding landscape. The analysed projects: Rudy House in Rudy, Shingle House in Bielsko-Biała, Modern Barn in the Żywiec Beskids and Natural Stone House in Borowiec, were subjected to formal, material and landscape analysis, and their facades were assessed in terms of their impact on the visual environment. The authors point to the importance of the theory of critical regionalism (Frampton), the phenomenology of architecture (Norberg-Schulz, Pallasmaa) and the aesthetics of sustainable architecture. The conclusions show that thanks to the use of local materials, subdued colors and textures corresponding to nature, it is possible to design modern architecture that does not dominate the landscape, but strengthens its identity.
